I have grown sorghum on this small plot near my home for many years. I will spread manure from my oxen and sheep before planting, and I managed to get some DAP and urea from the farmers' cooperative this season, though the supply came late and I did not receive as much as I hoped. I will use my own saved local seed because improved sorghum seed is difficult to find and too costly here in Tigray, and I do not plan to use any chemicals for pests since sorghum generally does well without them. My family will handle all the work on this 0.21-hectare plot ourselves—from ploughing with our oxen to planting, weeding, and harvesting—so we will not hire any outside labor.
